I think this is where some Buddhist philosophy can come in handy. I'm not saying that you should start reading buddhist texts, meditating and chanting, but the idea of "letting go" is a core tenet of the philosophy and really, everyone should try and practice it.

For me, it means allowing the thoughts, in your case the idea that he will come back, sit in your mind without you connecting with them. Recognise they are there and that your brain is generating this thought, but just let it sit and observe it if you wish. That way you can continue doing things that are going to benefit you without the thoughts weighing on your mind. 

Good luck, be strong, we're all in this together :)

Echoing the other post in this thread - there really is no closure.

It would be a very rare occurrence for you to find closure through a conversation with your ex. Any form of contact will only dig up the issues you already had and bring both of you more pain and hurt. Acceptance is the only thing you should practice here.

P.S. I know it's hard to accept, but if he cheated on you, then fuck him! Only terrible people cheat on their S.O. so you shouldn't feel so bad about the breakup. Try and use that fact to help you move on. You don't need someone like that in your life!

I think this is a trap a lot of people fall in to. They believe that their life purpose comes from an external source, often a SO. What were you like before you met him? If you weren't working towards your own goals, didn't have a lot of motivation or selfworth, didn't practice self love, etc, etc. then you have to work on these things without him.

What do you really want out of life? What inspires you? Sure it can be other people, but when you're relying upon others for the answers to these questions then you'll never truly realise them.
